name: focus-cards

frames.best_why: Right-hand photo is sharp with its title while the other five blur behind.

tagline: Photo grid where hovering one picture blurs the rest and names it.
summary: A three-by-two grid of landscape photo cards. Pointing at one keeps it sharp, darkens it with a white title, and blurs and shrinks the others.
appearance: A three-by-two grid of rounded landscape photo cards on black, each a different scene: mountains, a green valley, misty forest, desert rocks and coast. On hover the chosen card stays sharp while the rest blur and shrink slightly.
behaviour: Pointing at one photo blurs and slightly shrinks the other five and darkens the chosen card with a white title at its bottom-left. Moving away restores the whole grid.
demo_content: Six nature photos with titles like 'Above the clouds', 'Alpine valley' and 'Misty lake at dawn'.
search_phrases: photo grid that blurs other images on hover
hover one picture and dim the rest
card grid with title on hover
gallery where siblings go out of focus
case study image grid with blur
use_when: A set of six to nine images should let one stand out on hover without opening a lightbox.
avoid_when: The effect is hover-only, so touch users see a plain grid, and it needs photos of matching shape.
customise: Pass a cards array of title and image src and drop it into any container. The three-column breakpoint, blur amount and title styling are fixed.
weight_why: Six images with CSS blur and scale transitions; no script loop.

a11y.note: The focus effect and titles are hover-only, so keyboard users cannot reveal any title, and there is no reduced-motion check.

issues: Titles only appear on hover, so the grid is captionless at rest.
The first two hover frames show no title yet, only the blur change.
polish_why: Clean photo grid and a strong focus effect; titles are hover-only and easy to miss.
